title: POC scoping: sensitive flow retention & redaction - BlueHarbor Analytics
summary: Discovery + POC scoping for handling PII in prompts and logs. Discussed redaction, retention windows, scope of data stored for telemetry, benchmarking plan (replay vs synthetic), success criteria (latency SLOs, quality parity, auditability), and a two-week pilot timeline. Agreed to run a 7-day benchmark and provide security docs and a draft quote.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO whitepaper and KMS integration notes
Customer to provide sample anonymized prompt set (up to 5k examples)
Redwood SE to run preliminary latency/cost estimate and send draft quote
action_items: Maya Patel: Share security pack (SOC2 report, ISO docs, KMS/HSM integration guide) by 2026-12-23
Ethan Brooks: Prepare benchmark plan and synthetic workload config by 2026-12-28
Priya Iyer: Upload anonymized sample of 2–5k prompts to shared S3 test bucket by 2026-12-30
Carlos Mendez: Confirm pilot authority and procurement window (PO threshold) by 2027-01-03
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO), Priya (MLOps), Samir (Security)

Summary: quick scoping call focused on how BlueHarbor routes sensitive prompts through Redwood for a 2-week pilot. Main concerns: PII leakage in logs, configurable retention, redaction automation, and benchmark sizing.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros and then jump in. We're budgeting 45–60 minutes.
[00:12] Carlos: Hi, Carlos here. CTO. We're looking to test Redwood for our customer support summarization workflow which touches PHI/PII.
[00:20] Priya: Priya — lead on MLOps. We run approx 100k support interactions per month, average prompt length around 120 tokens, peaks are spikier. We're mostly worried about what gets stored and how to prove deletion.
[00:35] Ethan: thanks, yeah so from the platform side we support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For POC we usually start on Hosted with strict retention + redaction rules, or a Private control-plane if you need full network isolation.
[00:47] Samir: Quick — are you SOC 2 Type II? And what about key management, do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?
[00:55] Maya: Yes we are SOC2 and have an ISO pack. KMS integration is supported, HSM via our Private deployment — we'll send the docs.
[01:08] Carlos: Good. For the POC success criteria: 1) no raw PII in logs, 2) 95th pct latency under 200ms for the main route, 3) output quality parity with current pipeline — we'll use a fixed eval set.
[01:22] Priya: Also need audit logs that show retention and deletion events for prompt IDs. Right to Erasure is a blocker for us.
[01:33] Ethan: Understood. For redaction we have two approaches: automated inline redaction at ingestion (regex + ML PII classifier), or store hashed prompts and redact the stored copy on write. Both have tradeoffs — inline redaction reduces fidelity for debugging, hashed storage preserves raw tokens off of the main store but is irreversible unless you keep separate vaults.
[01:56] Carlos: Can you walk through an example? Say a prompt contains a SSN and a credit card number. What gets stored?
[02:04] Ethan: Sure. Option A (inline redaction): we scrub and replace detected tokens with <REDACTED> before logging; Option B (hash + ephemeral): we hash the prompt text (sha256) and store only the hash + derived metadata, while routing the raw prompt ephemeral directly to the model but not persisted past X seconds — this helps debugging if you keep ephemeral snapshots guarded by KMS, but it's more operational overhead.
[02:32] Priya: How good is the PII classifier? FPs/ FNs matter to us — a missed SSN is bad.
[02:39] Ethan: The built-in classifier is tuned for common PII types; we recommend a two-stage check: regex for high-confidence patterns (SSN/CC) and ML detector for contextual leaks. We can ship the classifier config used in the POC and you can fine-tune thresholds.
[02:58] Maya: On retention, we expose per-route retention windows: 0 days (no storage), 7 days, 30, 90, 365. You can also mark certain routes as ephemeral: logs are deleted after processing.
[03:12] Carlos: Do deletions provide proof? Audit trail?
[03:15] Ethan: Yes, deletions are recorded in audit logs with event IDs, timestamps, and the requesting principal. Those logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3.
[03:26] Samir: We need proofs for GDPR erasure — is the deletion immediate across all backups?
[03:30] Maya: For Hosted we provide logical deletion and scrub copies in standard backup windows; for legal-level guarantees we recommend Private where backups are customer-managed — we can detail RTO/RPO semantics in the security pack.
[03:44] Priya: Benchmarking — we want to understand latency and cost tradeoffs. Our target is approx 95th percentile <200ms and steady-state throughput ~30 requests/sec for the route.
[03:56] Ethan: For throughput/latency sizing we'll run two benchmarks: replay of your sample set (best) and synthetic traffic that simulates bursts. For replay we need ~2–5k representative prompts and target concurrency. We'll also test with quantized model variants to estimate cost delta.
[04:14] Carlos: What's the expected delta when using int8/quantized models vs full precision in terms of quality? We can't accept >3% drop in summary quality.
[04:22] Ethan: Quality delta depends on model family; for many Llama-based variants we've seen <2% drop on summarization tasks with 8-bit quantization if you tune temperature and sampling. We'll include a small human evaluation on your eval set.
[04:38] Priya: Can Redwood do prefix/KV cache so we get lower tail latency on repeated contexts? Our workflow reuses multiple customer context templates.
[04:46] Ethan: Yes, our runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching per route. That can cut median latency significantly for repeated tokens. We'll include that in the benchmark config.
[05:00] Carlos: For the pilot length — we prefer a 2-week pilot but operationally ok with a 7-day intensive benchmark followed by a 7-day softer integration run. Can Redwood support that timeline in early Jan?
[05:12] Maya: Yes, tentatively Jan 4th start for the 7-day benchmark, Jan 11–18 soft integration. We'll confirm.
[05:20] Samir: Can you also show redaction false positive logs? We need to see examples of when PII is redacted but it wasn't PII.
[05:28] Ethan: We'll capture FP/FN counts and example cases and surface them in the evaluation report.
[05:35] Priya: What about prompt storage for debugging — hashing means we can't replay exact prompts to reproduce issues. Any middle ground?
[05:42] Ethan: Middle ground is encrypted vaults: store raw prompts encrypted with your KMS key and access via RBAC only to approved engineers; deletion still triggers KMS-based wiping procedures. This gives replayability but increases compliance burden.
[06:00] Carlos: Procurement — quote needed. For POC we'd likely want a short-term reserved capacity with burst to Hosted. Any rough estimate for 100k monthly interactions?
[06:10] Maya: We'll run a back-of-envelope after we get sample prompts (token distribution) — Ethan will do an estimate and give a per-1M token estimate and possible Dedicated delta if you choose reserved capacity.
[06:22] Priya: Also, can we configure route-level retention to zero for certain user-facing routes (e.g., password reset flow)?
[06:30] Ethan: Yes, route-level policies are supported. You can attach policy tags like PII:HIGH -> retention=0 and logging=redact.
[06:38] Samir: Audit requirements — we need immutable logs, event signatures?
[06:42] Maya: Audit logs are append-only, stored with event signatures, and exported to your S3 or SIEM. For highest assurance we recommend Private so you manage storage retention end-to-end.
[06:55] Carlos: Ok let's align on success criteria again — latency <200ms 95p, FP/FN PII detection thresholds below 1%/2% respectively, evidence of deletion/audits, and a cost estimate under our target.
[07:12] Priya: We'll provide an eval set of 500 labelled examples for quality checks and 2–5k unlabeled prompts for replay.
[07:20] Maya: Great, here's what we'll do next — send security pack, benchmark plan, and a preliminary quote. We'll also include instructions for uploading prompts securely.
[07:32] Ethan: I'll prepare the synthetic workload template: concurrency, token distribution, KV-cache on/off scenarios, and quantization flags.
[07:40] Carlos: Thanks all — anything else?
[07:42] Priya: One more — can we get SLA terms for Dedicated if we scale?
[07:46] Maya: We'll include Dedicated SLA language in the quote addendum.
[07:50] Samir: Sounds good. End of call.

Meeting close.
